candidates.evidence: Four bands at 79.7, 104.4, 120.4 and 165.8 cm-1 with nothing clear above ~200 cm-1 is loosely consistent with the low-frequency Ag-type modes usually reported for CrI3 (~73, ~106, ~130, ~166 cm-1). The 166 and 104 matches are reasonable; the 80 and 120 bands are 7-10 cm-1 off the recalled values. Literature values are from memory and were not checked in the sandbox.

Recalled Td-WTe2 modes near ~112, ~135, ~165 and ~212 cm-1 would match the 165.8 band and the broad 104-120 cm-1 envelope. The expected ~212 cm-1 band is absent above noise, and the 120 cm-1 band sits ~15 cm-1 from the recalled ~135 cm-1 mode. Recalled, not verified.

Recalled GaTe A_g-type modes near ~113, ~134 and ~167 cm-1 partially match the 104-120 and 165.8 bands. The 104 band is ~9 cm-1 from the recalled 113 cm-1 mode, and no mode near 134 is significant in this fit. Recalled, not verified.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint null), so there is nothing to check against. The spectrum shows four significant low-frequency bands (79.7, 104.4, 120.4, 165.8 cm-1) and no significant signal above ~200 cm-1. The working-folder name contains 'AsI3', but I did not use it as evidence. As I recall it, AsI3 is a molecular crystal whose strongest Raman band is the As-I stretch near 200 cm-1, which is absent here, so the spectrum does not clearly match AsI3 either. That recall is uncertain. Identification is low confidence and should be confirmed with a reference spectrum or a literature database.

citations: Measured: spectrum.csv, despiked (8 single-pixel spikes replaced by 7-point median), 60-200 cm-1 Lorentzian fit, BIC comparison of 4/5/6-peak models (fit2.py, despiked.csv, overview.png in the working folder).

Literature (recalled from memory, not verified in this sandbox): CrI3 Raman at 532 nm, RT, approx. 73/106/130/166 cm-1 (e.g. Djurdjic-Mijin et al., PRB 98, 104307, 2018 - cited from memory, unverified).
Literature (recalled, not verified): WTe2 Td Raman approx. 112/135/165/212 cm-1; GaTe approx. 113/134/167 cm-1.
limits: Identification is low confidence. Four low-frequency bands (79.7, 104.4, 120.4, 165.8 cm-1) cannot be matched to one material with confidence from memory alone. No reference spectrum or literature database was available offline, so the candidate ranking rests on recalled values.
Absence of modes above ~200 cm-1 means not detected at this SNR. Noise is white with std ~650-1250 counts and clips to zero above ~600 cm-1, so weak modes could be hidden.
Weak features at ~127.6 cm-1 (shoulder, not significant by BIC), ~188 cm-1 (1.3 cm-1 wide, probably a residual spike) and ~215 cm-1 (noise level) are not reported as peaks.
The 104 cm-1 band (FWHM ~9) might be a doublet, but a 5-peak split model is not preferred by BIC, so this is unresolved.
No polarization or angle-resolved data, so symmetry labels (Ag/Eg etc.) cannot be assigned from measurement. Any irrep label is from recalled literature only.
Spike list is conservative: a 6-sigma robust threshold flagged 8 spikes. Weaker single-pixel spikes at ~342.6, 435.6, 493.4, 618.9, 667.7 and 888.9 cm-1 may also be artifacts and were not removed.
No Si substrate line at 520.7 cm-1 was found, so no substrate peak is reported.

Temperature 295 K and 532 nm are used as given. The working-folder name contains 'AsI3'; this was not used as evidence. The spectrum does not clearly match a molecular AsI3 crystal, as I recall its Raman bands, but that recall is uncertain. A reference spectrum of the stated material would settle the question.
